R240.note: Role check before the sink returns 403 for non-admins; the handler is documented as admin-only so the added restriction is the stated contract, and nothing else changes.

R241.note: setSecure(true) is the one-line fix for this sink; the response text still says 'secure flag set to: false' but that string was already there and is not a behaviour change.

R242.note: realpath plus separator-terminated containment closes the wrapper/traversal path, but the added single-component rule rejects subdirectory names like '2024/q1.txt' that the original served, and the un-canonicalised '__DIR__ . /reports' prefix would fail the containment compare on Windows and 404 every request.

R243.note: Named replacements with :startDate/:endDate placeholders parameterise the values through Sequelize; query shape and response unchanged.

R244.note: html/template with the same markup escapes both fields in text context and writes to the same ResponseWriter with the same error return; parsing the template per call is a cost, not an observable change.

R245.note: SandboxedEnvironment(autoescape=True) is the intended Jinja2 API for untrusted template source and keeps the 200/400 contract; the now-unused Environment import is left behind but harmless.

R246.note: Column allowlist is the right shape for an ORDER BY identifier, but an omitted or empty sort (previously a no-op in GORM) and any direction-bearing mode like 'total_cents desc' now error and surface as a 500 'report failed', and the write-up does not mention either.

R247.note: lockoutOnFailure: true closes the brute-force vector, but the unknown-user branch calls PasswordHasher.VerifyHashedPassword with '$2a$10$DECOY_HASH_PLACEHOLDER', which is not Base64 so Convert.FromBase64String throws FormatException: every mistyped username now 500s instead of showing 'Invalid login attempt', which is itself a user-enumeration oracle, and the write-up presents the branch as working.

R248.note: field_index >= MAX_FIELDS check before the read, returning the same -1 the other validation failures use; valid indices behave exactly as before.

R249.note: Extension allowlist is the correct shape for a denylist-bypass finding, but the chosen six types reject attachments the original accepted (.docx, .xlsx, .csv, .zip) with no contract calling for that set; the change is stated, so 1 not 0.

R250.note: encode_entities on both CGI values at the point of insertion; badge and structure untouched, and undef params warn exactly as the original concatenation did.

R251.note: proc_open array form with '--' closes both shell and option injection, but the original system() echoed ping's output into the response and the fix silently discards it, and the stdout/stderr pipes are closed before the child writes, which on Linux risks SIGPIPE-killing ping and reporting reachable hosts as false unless SIGPIPE is inherited as ignored.

R252.note: Direct !== 'premium' comparison removes string evaluation entirely; non-premium requests now throw where the PHP 7 default (assert.exception=0) only warned, but that enforcement is the documented contract and the write-up states the throw plainly.

R253.note: Argument-list Popen does not close this vector for a .bat on Windows: reproduced in a scratch dir on Python 3.13.12 where report_id 'x" & echo INJECTED>marker & "' still executed the echo via cmd.exe's re-parse of the batch command line; the docstring's alphanumeric-key contract calls for validation the fix omits, and nothing else about the function changed.
